problem: The phrase 'the depth the beam actually bends over' is unclear. A student may not see which of the two dimensions b and d must be squared, which is the whole point of the trap.
fix: Say it plainly: the squared dimension is the one measured perpendicular to the neutral axis, that is, in the direction of loading. For a plank laid flat, that is the 100 mm thickness, so Z = 200 × 100² / 6, not 100 × 200² / 6.

problem: The rectangle row writes 'Rectangle b × d' without saying that d is the dimension in the plane of bending and b the dimension parallel to the neutral axis. In the table the symbol d is also used for the diameter of the circle in the next two rows, so a reader skimming can carry the wrong meaning across.
fix: Label the row 'Rectangle, width b, depth d (d measured in the plane of bending, perpendicular to the neutral axis)' and keep I = bd³/12, y_max = d/2, Z = bd²/6.
